tasks.short: Meet the student board, review their plans, answer their questions with quoted university rules, sign forms and attend events.

steps.what: Teacher meets the board of the student organization
Teacher reviews the organization's event plans and budgets
Teacher answers the board's e-mailed questions about university rules

loop.input: The board's e-mailed question and the university's published rules for student organizations (events, safety, alcohol, funding).
loop.output: A draft reply quoting the matching rule with its link.
loop.check: Code checks every quote matches the rule text word for word; the teacher reads, edits and sends every reply.
loop.stop: One draft per question; no matching rule means the teacher writes the reply.
loop.why_not_simpler: Boards ask in their own words; rules are spread over several documents.

steps.what: Teacher signs paper forms for funding and room requests

tasks.design: For the board's e-mailed questions, a bounded step drafts replies that quote the university's published rules for student organizations, and the teacher edits and sends them. Funding and room requests come as e-forms that the teacher signs electronically ({ESIGN}) instead of on paper. Meetings, reviewing plans and attending events stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules were looked up for each question and forms signed on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: University rules are published online, and e-forms with e-signatures are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Boards change every year and need the same advice again.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a new board learn to run things without taking over.

reach.learn: Whether quoted rules cut repeat questions.

evidence.claim: University rules for student organizations are published online.
E-signatures on internal forms are valid when the signer is authenticated.

assumptions: Boundary: from board questions and plans to events attended; the organization's own decisions are outside.
Input contract: rules published by student affairs; e-forms set by student affairs; fallback is paper and lookup by hand.
Meetings, reviews and events do not change.
research_questions: How many questions match a published rule?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is meetings and judgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get candidate readings for the learning outcomes, check holdings and licences, format the list, select the final readings and publish them.

steps.what: Teacher searches catalogues and databases for specialized materials

loop.input: The course learning outcomes, the teacher's seed titles and results from the library catalogue and literature database searches.
loop.output: A candidate list with one line per title on the learning outcome it supports.
loop.check: Code keeps only titles that resolve by DOI or library catalogue record and drops the rest; the teacher reviews every candidate.
loop.stop: One list per course run; no new search rounds without the teacher.
loop.why_not_simpler: Matching titles to learning outcomes needs reading abstracts; keyword searches return too much.

steps.what: Teacher checks library holdings and licences for each title
Teacher formats the bibliography in the citation style
Teacher reads and selects the final readings for outside reading assignments
Teacher uploads the reading list to the course page

tasks.design: A bounded step proposes candidate readings from the library catalogue and literature databases ({OTHER}) per learning outcome, and code drops any title that does not resolve by DOI or catalogue record. The library's link resolver shows holdings and licences per title, and the reading-list tool formats the list. The teacher reads and selects the final readings; once selected, the list is published on the course page ({LMS}) with library links.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were searched, checked and formatted by hand each year.
tasks.enabler_now: Catalogues and link resolvers are queryable, and language models can match abstracts to learning outcomes.
tasks.still_hard: Models invent references; only resolved titles may pass.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which classic paper students should still struggle through.
tasks.altitude: The teacher selects from checked candidates instead of searching from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether resolved candidate lists cut librarian checks.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and foundational papers.
Chatbots can produce invented references that plagiarism checks do not flag.
Readings placed on a course page must stay within the institution's copyright licences.

assumptions: Boundary: from learning outcomes to the published list; buying new titles is outside.
Input contract: learning outcomes from the course guide; holdings and licences from the university library; fallback is searching by hand.
Librarian time is outside the teacher's savings.
research_questions: How many candidates does the teacher keep?

incremental.description: Teacher writes learning outcomes clearly enough to search on.

approvals.approved_version: The reading list as selected by the teacher in s4; changes need a new selection before publishing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Specialist fields with few databases save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher keeps advising students and choosing readings; rule lookups, paper forms and formatting go.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose reading lists are current every year without a weekend of searching.
